content.comment_body: As 2022 ends, it is still the case that [product_name] lacks an expansion module like PWM that could connect to modern small motor control modules. [product_name] struggles to execute calculations, process input signals, and provide accurate output, especially in slower contexts. When programs exceed 150 blocks, [product_name] can malfunction—inputs may not be read correctly and outputs may behave unpredictably, which can create hazardous conditions. This indicates a need for further product development.

In my experience, this is a good product. I use nearly 400 blocks without encountering delays or issues, but even 400 blocks aren't sufficient for my needs. AWS cloud services seem complex and are expensive, and payments are not very straightforward. I suggest [company_name] create its own cloud server, free of charge, making it simpler and more affordable to access [product_name] cloud services. This would certainly help boost sales. I'm also looking forward to seeing more advanced features in the latest version, such as integrated WiFi extender/repeater, an RS485 RTU Modbus server expansion module, faster loading for the web interface (whether due to memory card or communication speed), and a WiFi web camera that integrates smoothly with the new version. If possible, the new version could include a color LCD display to show graphics or images, which would be a valuable upgrade—acting as a mini HMI and displaying trends or other information.
It's likely that the price will stay the same, or maybe even decrease...

A $100 price point would be quite reasonable, if feasible. If an LCD screen is also a touch screen, mechanical keys could be eliminated. Free or affordable cloud services from [company_name] could help drive sales of [product_name] while also creating a new revenue stream. For context, Arduino is becoming popular with the Blynk platform to show dashboards on the cloud—their hardware and cloud fees are cheaper.
Everyone wants more features packed into [product_name], ideally without increasing the price—or even lowering it further.

Thank you for your response. What is the purpose of such a compact controller? While there are many web/cloud solutions for home or smart automation, the main function of this "programmable industrial controller" isn't really for those areas. Personally, I use it for equipment like circular saws, presses, automatic drills, casting robots, safety lighting, sewing devices, lifting gear, and more. These aren't toys or learning tools and generally have no use for internet/cloud integration or flashy features. The controller's key tasks are to read sensor data and control devices like solenoids, motor drives, and relays. Increasingly, basic control solutions are becoming difficult because modern motors no longer support simple 0-5V or 0-10V signals; PWM is now primary, and sometimes multiple channel encoders are needed. If outputs lag or malfunction, the situation becomes very challenging or even unsafe. If reliability is critical, options like [version_no] may be more appropriate. For example, a recent "smart machine" project on [product_name] plus HMI took three weeks for programming and testing; a similar project on [version_no] took more than three months—with professional developers—yielding the same outcome. This says a lot. As an example of problematic behavior: if the program stops or the machine isn't started from position zero, arbitrary numbers may display on HMI, motor drives may behave randomly, and the machine fails to recover on its own.

So you're looking for fast digital output? I agree—an expansion module with transistor output would also be useful. Machine control with [company_name] [product_name] seems more stable and reliable than Arduino-based controllers, and it is much easier to program.

Here is a thought: the Float/Int converter's output eAq isn't fully usable. If Aq returns 32767, there's no clear way to determine whether this is an overflow or a true value. Some kind of M flag or dedicated error detection block could help indicate overflow conditions.

I frequently use the Webcam function and find it very helpful. We manufacture OEM machines that serve customers on demand. If a problem occurs, the customer contacts our operation center, and the camera allows us to observe the issue and assist the client. This feature is a major benefit of [product_name]. While Amazon Cloud integration with the web editor is a nice addition, I agree that [company_name] should offer a more affordable alternative—Amazon is expensive, especially for hobbyists or large-scale projects.

I have attached examples of special functions available in other smart relay software (such as those from Schneider and Teco). Integrating such functions into [product_name] programming software would enable better configurations. Competitors offer more options, like 'Cam block' or sequential shift for managing multiple outputs, and an analog comparator for comparing timers, counters, registers, or analog inputs. I hope these suggestions can be taken into consideration to improve [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users provide a balanced view on [product_name] controllers, praising their utility yet criticizing limitations for industrial applications—notably the lack of PWM-compatible expansion modules and unreliable performance in more complex programs surpassing 150 blocks. Serious concerns arise about unpredictable I/O behavior, which may compromise safety in real machine operations. There are also calls for cloud connectivity enhancement, better web interfaces, upgraded display capabilities, faster data handling, and support for larger program sizes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect robust I/O performance for complex machine control projects and demand expansion modules, especially for PWM and motor integration. They also desire improvements in cloud connectivity, smoother programming interfaces, and more advanced display hardware. Affordability and ease of use are additional priorities.
